head: 17c0287fba8081896e1afc6c9be52d7e22bbe99d
reason: All three cases pass every review check. (1) Ground truth: all three use runtime_proof with a runtime_script, and each runtime/check.php was executed independently under php:8.3-cli and exits 0, confirming the stated behaviour (array_filter preserves keys yielding [1 => 1]; count() throws TypeError: Argument #1 ($value) must be of type Countable|array, Generator given; 'abc' == 0 evaluates to false). Citations verified against the cited php.net manual pages: array_filter documents 'Array keys are preserved, and may result in gaps'; count documents 'An array or Countable object' and the PHP 8.0 TypeError on invalid countable types; the comparison-operators page documents the PHP 7-to-8 change with 0 == 'a' going from true to false. (2) Expectations: every required predicate is specific (code + message_regex + exact line, lines verified against the fixtures: 22, 17, 15). No expectation was widened: the two Psalm false negatives (count-on-iterable, loose-comparison-with-zero) are recorded as findings, not acknowledged away. The allowed entries carry real reasons and were audited against raw output: Mago's impossible-condition (loose-comparison-with-zero) actually fires and is a correct diagnostic since the condition is runtime-proven always-false; PHPStan's deadCode.unreachable is dormant (PHPStan 2.3.1 reports only equal.alwaysFalse) and therefore excuses nothing. The notes' substantive tool-behaviour claims were independently reproduced with the pinned Psalm 6.20.0 phar: its callmap gives count() the signature Countable|array<array-key, mixed>, it reports InvalidArgument for Traversable and Generator parameters, PossiblyInvalidArgument for Countable|Traversable, and TypeDoesNotContainType for loose comparisons of two string literals and of two int literals - establishing that the Psalm silences are local gaps, not by-design divergences, and that the expected codes are the right ones. (3) Verdicts: all three cases were reproduced with python3 harness/bench.py run --case <id> and the raw tool output under results/runs/<run>/raw/ was read and matches the recorded verdicts and the notes: array-filter-string-callable-loses-list is green on all three tools (phpstan argument.type, psalm ArgumentTypeCoercion, mago possibly-invalid-argument, all at line 22); count-on-iterable is ok for phpstan/mago and false_negative for psalm; loose-comparison-with-zero is ok for phpstan/mago and false_negative for psalm. Tool versions in the runs match tools/versions.json (phpstan 2.3.1, psalm 6.20.0, mago 1.57.0) and the composer.json pins. (4) Contract: python3 harness/bench.py validate passes (18 cases, 0 invalid); composer.json is present in all three cases; git ls-tree at head shows no vendor/, .generated/ or scratch files committed (only harness-generated, gitignored vendor/autoload.php stubs exist on disk from the runs). Observation, not a defect: the three case additions landed in one commit, whereas AGENT-PROTOCOL rule 4 describes one concern per commit; this does not affect case correctness or any of the four review checks.
